quoted.text:
Meta vs Google:  many investors still keep forgetting that search and ads are 75%+ of Google’s revenues and 90%+ of profits.  Cloud and TPUs can’t make up for that.  So as personal agents take off, AI models won’t save Google and Gemini in the consumers app has to deliver.  

Currently Muse is a much superior personal agent and Gemini is stuck and not great as an agent (while the Carbon model is good on Vertex, even paid consumer users don’t have app access to it in the Gemini app or G-suite - I’m an Ultra subscriber and still am not getting Argon or Carbon, and that’s a major deployment failure for a new model where you have 1-2 weeks at most to win over users).  And the problem is structural and incentive driven - the Cloud and the API teams want Carbon access so consumers haven’t gotten it and Muse keeps getting better and improving while the Gemini app is stuck.

So the early trends suggest Meta wins the consumer agent market and the golden goose at Google (search and ads) is much more vulnerable than many expect.  I hope they get better at deploying and @joshwoodward can get new models out to consumers before they stop going to the Gemini app and build a habit to go to Muse.

To Gates, it was reportedly just a financial decision. But to Musk, it was something much deeper.

According to Naval, that moment revealed something fundamental about Elon Musk.

Elon Musk is not driven by money, wealth, or status. He is driven by a mission.

BREAKING: The US goods trade deficit widened by -$2.8 billion in September, or -2.1%, to -$134.9 billion, its widest gap since March 2025.

Imports rose +$8.1 billion, or +2.4%, to a record $344.2 billion.

This jump was led by a +7.5% MoM increase in capital goods, which include computers and accessories, semiconductors, and telecommunications equipment fueling the AI buildout.

Now, the capital goods deficit has widened by -$54.3 billion YoY, accounting for more than the entire increase in the overall trade deficit.

Meanwhile, US goods exports jumped +$5.3 billion in September, or +2.6%, to $209.2 billion, driven by a +12.8% increase in food shipments.

The US trade deficit is rapidly widening again.

posts.name: Mark Cuban
posts.text:
Multiple roommates.  Ramen noodles.  Near public transportation.  Respect to the people who do whatever it takes.  

I worked as a bartender.  Bar-back. $2.15 an hr plus whatever tips got shared.  Worked at a retail store. Never had benefits at any job.  

Had 5 roommates in a 3 br apt.  Ate lousy food out of cans and ate  a ton of peanuts and shit food  at happy hour.  Had credit cards ripped up.  Etc.  

But I learned a ton.  Taught me what was right and wrong about running a business by watching my bosses and their bosses 

Yeah I know. It was much easier then, when inflation was 15 pct and national unemployment was 10 %.  I know I was fortunate when I finally got fired from the store, and had to start my own business with zero cash.   Bill collectors everywhere. 
Even luckier when I found my first customer so I could pay my bills

But I recognize it’s so much harder today.  

Which is why I respect the people who are willing to do what it takes to get started

posts.name: Steve Burns
posts.text:
One of the most useful things to measure after earnings isn't the size of the gap.

Measure how much of that gap survives.
A stock that gaps 12% and keeps 11% has processed the new information very differently from one that gaps 12% and finishes up 2%.

The announcement creates the gap.
The price action afterward tells you what traders ultimately decided about the move.
